knowledge_point.title: Solving for Three Coefficients in a Linear Combination

question.:question/problem:
Consider the vectors

$$
a_1=\begin{bmatrix}1 \\ 3 \\ -2\end{bmatrix},\quad a_2=\begin{bmatrix}-3 \\ -8 \\ 6\end{bmatrix},\quad a_3=\begin{bmatrix}2 \\ 5 \\ -3\end{bmatrix},\quad b=\begin{bmatrix}11 \\ 31 \\ -22\end{bmatrix}
$$

If $x_1a_1+x_2a_2+x_3a_3=b,$ then what is $x_{1} + x_{2} + x_{3}?$
question.:question/worked-solution:
If $x_1a_1+x_2a_2+x_3a_3=b$, then we have

$$
\begin{aligned}x_1\begin{bmatrix}1 \\ 3 \\ -2\end{bmatrix}+x_2\begin{bmatrix}-3 \\ -8 \\ 6\end{bmatrix}+x_3\begin{bmatrix}2 \\ 5 \\ -3\end{bmatrix}&=\begin{bmatrix}11 \\ 31 \\ -22\end{bmatrix} \\ \begin{bmatrix}x_{1} \\ 3 x_{1} \\ - 2 x_{1}\end{bmatrix}+\begin{bmatrix}- 3 x_{2} \\ - 8 x_{2} \\ 6 x_{2}\end{bmatrix}+\begin{bmatrix}2 x_{3} \\ 5 x_{3} \\ - 3 x_{3}\end{bmatrix}&=\begin{bmatrix}11 \\ 31 \\ -22\end{bmatrix} \\ \begin{bmatrix}x_{1} - 3 x_{2} + 2 x_{3} \\ 3 x_{1} - 8 x_{2} + 5 x_{3} \\ - 2 x_{1} + 6 x_{2} - 3 x_{3}\end{bmatrix}&=\begin{bmatrix}11 \\ 31 \\ -22\end{bmatrix}\end{aligned}
$$

Equating the corresponding components, we get the following system:

$$
\left\{\begin{aligned}x_{1} - 3 x_{2} + 2 x_{3} &=11 \\ 3 x_{1} - 8 x_{2} + 5 x_{3} &=31 \\ - 2 x_{1} + 6 x_{2} - 3 x_{3} &=-22\end{aligned}\right.
$$

We will solve this system using Gaussian elimination. First, we write the augmented matrix for this system:

$$
M=\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & -3 & 2 & 11 \\ 3 & -8 & 5 & 31 \\ -2 & 6 & -3 & -22\end{array}\right]
$$

Row-reducing the augmented matrix, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}M&=\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & -3 & 2 & 11 \\ 3 & -8 & 5 & 31 \\ -2 & 6 & -3 & -22\end{array}\right] \\ &\sim \left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & -3 & 2 & 11 \\ 0 & 1 & -1 & -2 \\ -2 & 6 & -3 & -22\end{array}\right] && R_{2}:=R_{2}+(-3)R_{1} \\ &\sim \left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & -3 & 2 & 11 \\ 0 & 1 & -1 & -2 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 & 0\end{array}\right] && R_{3}:=R_{3}+(2)R_{1}\end{aligned}
$$

The system is now

$$
\left\{\begin{aligned}x_{1} - 3 x_{2} + 2 x_{3} &=11 \\ x_{2} - x_{3} &=-2 \\ x_{3} &=0\end{aligned}\right.
$$

From the third equation, we get $x_3=0.$ Substituting this value into the second equation, we get

$$
1x_2+(-1)(0)=-2\quad\Rightarrow\quad x_2=-2
$$

Finally, substituting these values into the first equation, we obtain

$$
x_1+(-3)(-2)+(2)(0)=11\quad\Rightarrow\quad x_1=5
$$

So, the solution of the system is $x_1=5$, $x_2=-2$, $x_3=0$, which means

$$
5a_1+(-2)a_2+(0)a_3=b.
$$

Consequently,

$$
x_{1} + x_{2} + x_{3}=(5)+(-2)+(0)=3.
$$

knowledge_point.title: Solving for Three Coefficients in a Linear Combination

question.:question/problem:
Consider the vectors

$$
a_1=\begin{bmatrix}1 \\ 0 \\ 3\end{bmatrix},\quad a_2=\begin{bmatrix}-1 \\ 0 \\ -1\end{bmatrix},\quad a_3=\begin{bmatrix}2 \\ 5 \\ 1\end{bmatrix},\quad b=\begin{bmatrix}-16 \\ -30 \\ -8\end{bmatrix}
$$

If $x_1a_1+x_2a_2+x_3a_3=b,$ then what is $x_{1} + x_{2} + x_{3}?$
question.:question/worked-solution:
If $x_1a_1+x_2a_2+x_3a_3=b$, then we have

$$
\begin{aligned}x_1\begin{bmatrix}1 \\ 0 \\ 3\end{bmatrix}+x_2\begin{bmatrix}-1 \\ 0 \\ -1\end{bmatrix}+x_3\begin{bmatrix}2 \\ 5 \\ 1\end{bmatrix}&=\begin{bmatrix}-16 \\ -30 \\ -8\end{bmatrix} \\ \begin{bmatrix}x_{1} \\ 0 \\ 3 x_{1}\end{bmatrix}+\begin{bmatrix}- x_{2} \\ 0 \\ - x_{2}\end{bmatrix}+\begin{bmatrix}2 x_{3} \\ 5 x_{3} \\ x_{3}\end{bmatrix}&=\begin{bmatrix}-16 \\ -30 \\ -8\end{bmatrix} \\ \begin{bmatrix}x_{1} - x_{2} + 2 x_{3} \\ 5 x_{3} \\ 3 x_{1} - x_{2} + x_{3}\end{bmatrix}&=\begin{bmatrix}-16 \\ -30 \\ -8\end{bmatrix}\end{aligned}
$$

Equating the corresponding components, we get the following system:

$$
\left\{\begin{aligned}x_{1} - x_{2} + 2 x_{3} &=-16 \\ 5 x_{3} &=-30 \\ 3 x_{1} - x_{2} + x_{3} &=-8\end{aligned}\right.
$$

We will solve this system using Gaussian elimination. First, we write the augmented matrix for this system:

$$
M=\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & -1 & 2 & -16 \\ 0 & 0 & 5 & -30 \\ 3 & -1 & 1 & -8\end{array}\right]
$$

Row-reducing the augmented matrix, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}M&=\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & -1 & 2 & -16 \\ 0 & 0 & 5 & -30 \\ 3 & -1 & 1 & -8\end{array}\right] \\ &\sim \left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & -1 & 2 & -16 \\ 0 & 0 & 5 & -30 \\ 0 & 2 & -5 & 40\end{array}\right] && R_{3}:=R_{3}+(-3)R_{1} \\ &\sim \left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & -1 & 2 & -16 \\ 0 & 2 & -5 & 40 \\ 0 & 0 & 5 & -30\end{array}\right] && R_{2}\leftrightarrow R_{3} \\ &\sim \left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & -1 & 2 & -16 \\ 0 & 1 & - \frac{5}{2} & 20 \\ 0 & 0 & 5 & -30\end{array}\right] && R_{2}:=\left(\frac{1}{2}\right)R_{2} \\ &\sim \left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & -1 & 2 & -16 \\ 0 & 1 & - \frac{5}{2} & 20 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 & -6\end{array}\right] && R_{3}:=\left(\frac{1}{5}\right)R_{3}\end{aligned}
$$

The system is now

$$
\left\{\begin{aligned}x_{1} - x_{2} + 2 x_{3} &=-16 \\ x_{2} - \frac{5 x_{3}}{2} &=20 \\ x_{3} &=-6\end{aligned}\right.
$$

From the third equation, we get $x_3=-6.$ Substituting this value into the second equation, we get

$$
1x_2+\left(- \frac{5}{2}\right)(-6)=20\quad\Rightarrow\quad x_2=5
$$

Finally, substituting these values into the first equation, we obtain

$$
x_1+(-1)(5)+(2)(-6)=-16\quad\Rightarrow\quad x_1=1
$$

So, the solution of the system is $x_1=1$, $x_2=5$, $x_3=-6$, which means

$$
1a_1+(5)a_2+(-6)a_3=b.
$$

Consequently,

$$
x_{1} + x_{2} + x_{3}=(1)+(5)+(-6)=0.
$$
